model: cost_model_151 (cost_model_141 version 4, revision 2, with follow-up pages shared among workers)

runs_per_month.source: twice weekly (the client's requirement; the shipped schedule: Tuesday and Friday, off)

schedule_interval_hours.source: twice weekly at 06:00 store time; a run longer than 72 h makes the next occurrence start nothing (on_overlap: continue), so the cadence drops, never the scope

oxylabs_usd_per_1000_results.source: oxylabs_web_api_pricing_read_20261028.md: no Walmart row; 'Scrape (from)' 0.50, 'Other targets' and 'Custom domain non-JS' 1.00 (first two bands), 'Custom domain JS' 1.50 (the collector's reserve of USD 0.0015 a result)

oxylabs_plans.source: the band limits of the 'Scrape (from)', 'Other targets' and 'Custom domain JS' rows; the page says nothing about overage or pay-as-you-go: a volume above a band is priced at the next plan; above Enterprise's band, a quote

scrapedo_plans.source: scrapedo_pricing_read_20261028.md (monthly price, credits, concurrent requests); requests stop at the monthly limit; annual billing: pay 10 months for 12

scrapedo_credits_per_page.source: the campaign's ledger (Scrape.do-Request-Cost answer header): result pages and follow-up product pages through /plugin/walmart/store 10; UPC product pages, robots.txt and the store page through the general API 1; a Walmart 404 is charged; failed store-endpoint requests are free

shipped_configuration.source: config/collector.yaml of 37ffca8 (ParallelConfig: workers and max_in_flight 1 to 8)

distinct_pickup_products_N.source: not measured: no run read the full scope. 20k to 80k brackets a supercenter's Pickup assortment in the 11 required CSV rows; 120k is the 1.2.1 figure, kept only for comparison (it described Walmart's unfiltered online catalogue, scope_audit_141.py). A census (one result page per root listing, about 615 pages) would read each root's Pickup total: their sum bounds N from above (a product under several roots counts once per root) and fixes the result pages of a full run

cases.source: overlap: result pages read per (N / valid products per page), for products listed in several root listings, partitions of listings Walmart does not serve to the end, and partial last pages (measured on small runs only, see measured.overlap_in_runs); variant candidates (siblings a tile names and no tile of the run shows) per product: measured 0.78 to 1.54 on bounded runs, expected lower at full scope where more siblings have their own tile, so 0.5 to 1.0; sponsored-only products per product: measured 0.03 to 0.18 on bounded runs (an upper reference: at full scope most sponsored products also appear organically); new products per run: 1.2.1 assumed 10 %, 2 % is the lean case; charged retries: lean = the campaign's measured share, heavy = the 1.3.1 allowance of 10 %; offer pages: none as shipped (offers are read from the pages already read; 0 deal candidates in 5,470 tiles), heavy = a product page re-read every run for 2 % of products; interruptions: each re-sends the requests in flight (one per worker)

follow_up_reuse_of_exclusions.source: as shipped (walmart.py follow_up of 37ffca8) every candidate a run names is read in that run, whatever an earlier run decided; the design option, not implemented, reuses an exclusion (out of scope, no local offer) for the 30-day reuse period, while included candidates are read in every run (their price must be fresh)

retention_policy.source: no retention policy is configured or approved: the stored pages of the last 2 runs, 90 days of observations in the database (records kept indefinitely), and the last 2 database dumps

collector_seconds_per_request_besides_th.source: run D's one-worker segments: span per request minus the mean answer time (0.33, 0.30, 0.31 s)

throughput_requests_per_min_per_worker.kind: measured (Scrape.do follow-ups and the fast end of its result pages: estimated from answer times)
throughput_requests_per_min_per_worker.source: THROUGHPUT_1_4_1.csv: segments of 2026-10-28 with at least 20 requests, by stage; workers 1, 2 and 4 measured (4 is the most measured; the configuration allows 8, not measured: the hours with 8 workers assume the per-worker rates hold); the follow-up stage runs one task per kind, so one worker per kind. Scrape.do: follow-up pages 60 / (answer time + collector time) from its 5 follow-up pages (mean and median); result pages: B2's segment (slow end) and the median answer time of its 49 result pages (fast end)

charged_retry_share_measured.source: requests with a charge (or a reservation kept: possibly charged) and no usable answer, per answered request, all live runs of 2026-10-28: Oxylabs 16 of 1159, Scrape.do 15 of 494 (Walmart 404s, 1 credit each); free failures (time only): Oxylabs 15, Scrape.do 2

valid_products_per_result_page.source: Oxylabs runs B2 (1.4.0) and B3 (1.4.1), Pickup grid, no follow-up and no UPC page: valid fresh products per result page read, pooled over the two runs: B2 675/19; B3 662/19; together 1337/38

follow_up_outcomes_phase_D.source: run D (01M60VA5, 1.4.1, variant follow-ups of 5 listings): coverage follow_up_outcomes

stored_bytes_per_page.source: live.tar of runs B1, B2, B3 and D (gzip-compressed files, as stored on the VM)

database_bytes_per_observation.source: walmart_oxylabs on 2026-10-28T10:22Z (command 367): 53,410,839 bytes for 3,208 product observations, 3,733 records and 963 page fetches (with their events and ledger); an order of magnitude only, never measured at production scale

export_bytes_per_exported_row.source: the B3 and D export folders (products, provenance, record map, memberships, offers, coverage) per row

what_it_was.model: cost_model_131 (version 3), scenario central/F0, a later month
what_it_was.azure: VM USD 62 to 67 (collection hours) + data disk E15 19.20 + OS disk 2.40 + IP 3.65

why_withdrawn: scope: its 36,000 result pages a run and 120,000 products described Walmart's unfiltered online assortment (the Scrape.do store endpoint without the Pickup filter, 947 links counted as independent listings although 315 of the 945 named are nested in another listed listing); the configured scope is store #3891's Pickup assortment, whose measured totals are 1.7 % to 6.9 % of the unfiltered totals in the 5 non-produce listings measured both ways (Bath & Body, Shampoo, Laundry, Diapering, Dry Dog Food; for example Bath & Body 2,881 to 2,897 against 108,395 to 110,434, Diapering 512 to 515 against 30,534 to 30,749)
it left out the follow-ups (sponsored-only products and variant siblings) the requirements include; with them, the same model put a later run above the 72-hour interval and the volume in Enterprise
the reply gave a monthly figure only; the report's one-time first run (about 6 to 6.5 days with two workers, during which the twice-weekly occurrences start nothing) was not in the reply

the Oxylabs rate is not published for Walmart: USD 1.00 per 1,000 is one reading of the price page (USD 0.50 to 1.50 per 1,000 are possible), and the plan steps (USD 100, 500, 2,500) dominate the bill
its run time assumed at most two requests at once; four workers were measured on 2026-10-28, and the follow-up stage (one task per kind) was found to be the limit of a full run
an estimate, never an invoice or a quote
